topics.title: Underperformance
questions: What observable facts show the performance gap?
Was the standard clearly understood and realistically achievable?
Is the primary factor skill, clarity, capacity, motivation, process, relationship, or context?
topics.framework: Address specific behavior and results rather than personality. Explain impact, invite perspective, diagnose contributing factors, clarify the required standard, and agree on support plus a review date.
actions: Set one measurable commitment and follow-up date

topics.title: Chronic lateness and attendance
questions: What pattern can be documented?
What operational or team impact is occurring?
Was the schedule standard explicit?
topics.framework: Address the pattern promptly and privately. Focus on observable attendance behavior and impact, invite perspective, restate the standard, and follow organizational policy consistently.
actions: Agree on next steps and review consistently

topics.title: Employee coaching
questions: What outcome does the employee want?
What capability would make the greatest difference?
What options has the employee considered?
topics.framework: Use questions before advice. Help the employee clarify the goal, current reality, options, and a self-authored commitment.

topics.title: Difficult conversations
questions: What shared outcome should anchor the discussion?
Which facts can be observed directly?
What response are you prepared to hear?
topics.framework: Open with purpose, describe observations without labels, explain impact, invite perspective, clarify expectations, and close with an explicit agreement.

topics.title: Feedback
questions: What was the specific situation?
What behavior was observed?
What impact occurred?
topics.framework: Keep feedback timely and specific. Separate observation from interpretation and connect behavior to impact and a future request.
actions: Describe behavior like a camera would
Ask for an actionable future behavior

topics.title: Accountability
questions: Was the commitment unambiguous?
Who owns the outcome?
What evidence and review date were agreed?
topics.framework: Accountability requires a clear owner, observable deliverable, deadline, support, and consistent review without blame.

topics.title: Delegation
questions: What outcome can be transferred?
What authority and guardrails are appropriate?
What checkpoints replace constant monitoring?
topics.framework: Delegate an outcome rather than a script. Define authority, constraints, resources, evidence, and milestone reviews.

topics.title: Conflict
questions: What is the actual point of disagreement?
What shared outcome exists?
Which interests and evidence differ?
topics.framework: State the issue neutrally, distinguish positions from interests, protect respect, and agree on a decision or resolution process.

topics.title: Psychological safety
questions: What happens when someone challenges an idea?
Which leader behavior may silence concerns?
How are mistakes reviewed?
topics.framework: Invite concerns and dissent while maintaining high standards. Thank people for raising risks and separate learning reviews from blame.

topics.title: Change leadership
questions: What might stakeholders believe they are losing?
What is known, unknown, and next?
What behavior proves adoption?
topics.framework: Diagnose resistance before persuading. Clarify purpose, tradeoffs, participation, support, communication cadence, and evidence of adoption.

topics.title: Executive presence
questions: What must the audience understand or decide?
What evidence and tradeoff matter most?
What can be removed?
topics.framework: Credibility comes from clear thinking, composure, concise communication, and reliable follow-through.

topics.title: Healthcare clinical leadership
questions: What patient, workforce, quality, or operational outcome is involved?
Which professional roles and expertise must be included?
What issue requires escalation through safety or clinical channels?
topics.framework: Use interprofessional role clarity, respectful communication, shared goals, situation awareness, mutual support, and proper organizational safety processes.
actions: Escalate clinical or safety issues through qualified channels

topics.title: Healthcare team handoffs
questions: Where is information lost?
Who needs closed-loop confirmation?
What role or scope assumption is unclear?
topics.framework: Strengthen handoffs through clear ownership, concise shared information, check-backs, and explicit escalation paths.

topics.title: Higher education shared governance
questions: What decision rights or governance process applies?
Whose expertise and voice are needed?
How does the issue connect to mission and student success?
topics.framework: Distinguish consultation, recommendation, and decision authority. Build process credibility through transparency, inclusion, and follow-through.
actions: Explain how input shaped the decision

topics.title: Higher education performance
questions: What standard, appointment expectation, or role responsibility applies?
What evidence is available?
Which institutional process must be followed?
topics.framework: Address observable performance while respecting role, governance, policy, and due-process requirements. Involve qualified institutional resources for consequential action.
actions: Combine support with a review date

topics.title: Family enterprise roles
questions: Is this a family, ownership, or management issue?
Which forum should handle it?
Who has decision authority?
topics.framework: Separate family, ownership, and business roles. Clarify forums, standards, decision rights, and boundaries.
actions: Name the role each person is speaking from
Move the issue to the correct forum

topics.title: Succession planning
questions: What readiness evidence is required?
How will authority transfer become visible?
What knowledge and relationships must transfer?
topics.framework: Treat succession as a staged process involving readiness, authority, knowledge, relationships, governance, contingency planning, and stakeholder communication.
actions: Create emergency and planned succession milestones

topics.title: Family employee performance
questions: Would the same standard apply to a non-family employee?
Which role is being discussed: family, owner, or employee?
Who should conduct the performance conversation?
topics.framework: Use consistent business standards while protecting family relationships through clear role boundaries and the appropriate governance forum.
actions: Use an impartial reviewer when appropriate

topics.title: 360 feedback
questions: Which observable behavior should be rated?
What examples support the rating?
What strength and development priority emerge?
topics.framework: Use observable behaviors across Leading Self, Relationships, Teams, Performance, Change, and the System. Avoid personality labels and require examples.

topics.title: Meetings and team effectiveness
questions: What output must exist when the meeting ends?
Who is needed and who owns the decision?
Which norm would improve participation?
topics.framework: Design meetings for decisions, coordination, learning, or relationships. Clarify purpose, roles, decision method, actions, owners, and dates.

simulations.title: Underperformance
simulations.opening: I want to discuss a pattern I have observed because it is affecting our shared outcomes. I will explain what I have seen, then I want to understand your perspective.
employee_replies: I do not think this is a problem.
There are factors you do not understand.
I will work on it.
leader_moves: Return to observable facts
Acknowledge the perspective and diagnose barriers
Clarify expectations, support, evidence, and review date
